title: 1 Kings 3
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon made an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. He brought her to the City of David while he was still finishing his palace, the temple of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem. ² The people, however, were still sacrificing at the high places, because no temple had yet been built for the name of the LORD. ³ Solomon showed his love for the LORD by living according to the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places. ⁴ The king went to Gibeon to offer sacrifices, for that was the most important high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar. ⁵ At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at night and said, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."

⁶ Solomon said, "You showed great faithfulness to your servant David my father, because he walked before you in truth, in righteousness, and with an undivided heart. And you have continued to show him this great kindness by giving him a son to sit on his throne today. ⁷ Now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David, yet I am just a young man and don't know how to carry out my duties. ⁸ Your servant is among your chosen people, a great people too numerous to count or number. ⁹ Give your servant a discerning heart to govern your people and to distinguish between right and wrong — for who is able to govern this great people of yours?" ¹⁰ It pleased the LORD that Solomon had asked for this.

¹¹ God said to him, "Since you have asked for this — since you have not asked for long life or wealth for yourself, or for the death of your enemies, but have asked for discernment in administering justice — ¹² I will do what you have asked. I am giving you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been anyone like you before, and there never will be after you. ¹³ Moreover, I am giving you what you did not ask for — both riches and honor — so that in your lifetime no other king will compare with you. ¹⁴ And if you walk in my ways and obey my statutes and commands as your father David did, I will give you a long life." ¹⁵ Then Solomon woke up and realized it had been a dream. He returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he gave a feast for all his servants.

¹⁶ Now two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him. ¹⁷ One of them said, "Pardon me, my lord. This woman and I live in the same house, and I had a baby while she was there with me. ¹⁸ The third day after my child was born, she gave birth too. We were alone in the house — just the two of us, no one else. ¹⁹ During the night this woman's son died because she rolled over on him. ²⁰ She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was sleeping. She put him at her breast and put her dead son next to me.

²¹ When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning light, I could see he was not the son I had given birth to." ²² The other woman said, "No! The living child is mine, and the dead one is yours." The first retorted, "No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine." They argued back and forth before the king. ²³ The king said, "One of you claims, 'My son is alive and your son is dead,' while the other claims, 'No, your son is dead and mine is alive.'" ²⁴ He then said, "Bring me a sword." A sword was brought to him. ²⁵ "Cut the living child in two," the king ordered, "and give half to one woman and half to the other."

²⁶ At this, the woman whose son was alive was overcome with grief for her child and cried out to the king, "Please, my lord, give her the living baby! Don't kill him!" But the other said, "Neither of us will have him — go ahead and cut him in two." ²⁷ Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the living baby to the first woman. Don't kill him. She is his mother." ²⁸ When all Israel heard the verdict the king had given, they held the king in great awe. They saw that he had wisdom from God to administer justice.
